newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela external debt $25.44 bln at end of '96.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela external debt $25.44 bln at end of '96.

text.p: Venezuela lowered its total stock of external debt to $25.443 billion at the end of 1996 from $26.901 billion at the end of 1995, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said, and the country is up to date with its debt payments.
"We're still behind just $30 million, due to legal reasons, but that should be settled by the end of the month," Matos told the Senate Finance Comission.
Matos said debt arrears had fallen from $162 million at the end of 1996, $418 million at the end of 1995 and $499 million at the end of 1994.
This year and the next were the hardest in terms of debt servicing, he added, but Venezuela has been approached by 20 international banks to find ways to restructure the country's debt profile.
"We're looking along similar lines that Mexico and the Phillipines have taken," he said.
Matos recently had talks in New York with bankers to hear their ideas on how to best restructure Venezuela's debt profile.
